global_caption: The video contains 3 shots. It is a museum physics interactive exhibit safety shattering demonstration rendered in a neutral-toned watercolor illustration style. The overall visual tone uses soft ambient gallery lighting and subtle glass reflections as a consistent lighting base. No background Overall mood centers on tension and passionate intensity.
shot1: Shot 1 serves as the opening shot, starting with a wide eye-level view. The camera slowly dollies in from the entrance of the museum physics interactive exhibit. Foreground features low-saturation display board edges and semi-transparent signage; background includes softly lined interactive equipment and sparse visitors. The subject, a young man with shounen anime traits, walks into the center of the frame and stops before the protective platform. Composition uses cabinet edges and floor lines to guide the viewer’s gaze toward the sealed transparent sphere on the platform. Shallow depth of field keeps both the character and device sharp while slightly blurring the background crowd. Soft light evenly fills the hall, with gentle reflections on glass surfaces but no glare. the second half lands precisely on the moment his lips curl upward and his finger freezes.
shot2: Shot 2 connects to the previous shot via a hard cut, transitioning to a close-up side angle. The camera quickly pans near one side of the protective shield, shifting focus rapidly from the steel ball’s trajectory to the surface of the transparent sphere. Composition places the curved shield surface in the foreground as a natural frame, mid-ground shows the impact point, and background features subdued audience area and gallery light strips. Under consistent neutral tones and soft lighting, sharper highlights appear at the moment of impact. The instant the steel ball strikes the sphere, the transition from intact to crack propagation to full explosion is fully recorded. Fragments of varying sizes eject outward along different arcs. Larger shards initially rush toward the shield before slowing and sliding down, while finer particles briefly shimmer with translucent quality under the lights. Multiple collision trails and fine scratches are clearly visible on the inner surface of the shield. Clothing edges and hair strands subtly flutter due to the subject’s sudden forward lean. The camera pauses briefly at the densest cluster of trajectories, emphasizing “破碎路径” as a key visual element.
shot3: Shot 3 continues with another hard cut into the closing segment, using an extreme close-up overhead view with a slow pull-out. Filming starts from the ground safety observation zone. Foreground shows clearly marked landing lines and numbers; focus rests on scattered fragments and several typical arc patterns. Mid-ground features the young man crouching, hand reaching close to the ground without touching the danger boundary. Background includes the base of the protective platform and blurred human silhouettes. Lighting remains soft and diffused, with only minimal cool glass reflections preserved on fragment edges, allowing lines and color blocks in the watercolor style to feel both controlled and dynamic. As the camera slowly pulls back, it re-incorporates the character, ground markings, fragment landing points, and protective platform into a single frame, ultimately freezing on a complete and readable ejection distribution map, concluding with the experiment result clearly observed and displayed.
